title: A Robot as an Interface: Drive, ArmBus and LegBus, and a Fake That Behaves Like the Hardware

questions.question: Why write the interface before the hardware?
options: So that the program is written against the class and the simulator, a fake and a board are interchangeable
questions.explanation: The program should not know which robot it is on.

questions.question: A base with a limit of 1 m/s was told to go 5 m/s. After 10 s it was doing:
questions.explanation: A fake that does not limit teaches a program to ask for the impossible.

questions.question: What did a stop at 1 m/s cost in distance for a time constant of 0.2 s?
options: 0.200 m, the speed times the time constant

questions.question: How long did three joints at 0.5 rad/s take to move 1 rad, and twelve at 2 rad/s?
questions.explanation: The time is the distance over the rate.

questions.question: A controller is tuned on a fake that answers instantly. What happens on the real base?
options: It is tuned for a robot that does not exist and overshoots on the real one
questions.explanation: A fake that is too kind teaches bad habits.

questions.question: Why are ArmBus and LegBus separate types when they are the same row of joints?
options: So a program cannot hand an arm's targets to a leg
questions.explanation: A type is a mistake that cannot be made.
